## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 00f9da2de0f662b4105b134e9f4c568c2a0e8e35

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation.** I traced the full history of `KeychainDatabase.java`'s `onUpgrade()` switch, since the fix only touches case-label numbers (shifting case 8→15 down to 7→14 and merging case 7/8). The switch has a clear convention established from its first versions: when `DATABASE_VERSION` is bumped from `N` to `N+1`, exactly **one** new `case N:` block is added (confirmed in the `1→2`, `3→4`, `4→5`, `5→6`, `6→7`, `8→9`, `9→10`, ... bump commits). Because none of these `case` blocks ever `break`, execution always falls through from the matching `case` to the end of the switch — so the label only matters for *where entry starts*, not whether code eventually executes.

I then scanned every commit touching this file and counted, for each `DATABASE_VERSION` bump, how many new `case N:` labels were added. All of them added exactly one new case — except one.

**(2) The specific change.** Commit `00f9da2de0f662b4105b134e9f4c568c2a0e8e35` (Jan 29 2015, "add table for allowed key ids in API") bumps `DATABASE_VERSION` from 7 to 8, but adds **two** new case labels instead of one:
```java
case 7:
    // consolidate
case 8:
    // new table for allowed key ids in API
    try { db.execSQL(CREATE_API_APPS_ALLOWED_KEYS); } ...
```
Per the established convention, this single version bump should have added only `case 7:` containing the new SQL. Instead it introduced a spurious empty `case 7:` and pushed the real migration code to `case 8:`. Every subsequent version bump (8→9, 9→10, ... 14→15) correctly added just one new case each, but all of them inherited the +1 offset, so the last real migration (adding `name`/`email`/`comment` columns, added when bumping 14→15) ended up mislabeled `case 15:` instead of `case 14:`.

The practical consequence: a user whose local DB was exactly at version 8 (a real, released version — DATABASE_VERSION=8 was in production for about a month, Jan 29–Mar 2015) would, on a later upgrade, enter the switch directly at the mislabeled `case 8:`, re-executing the `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS certs; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS user_ids; CREATE_USER_PACKETS; CREATE_CERTS` step that was actually meant only for the one-time 7→8 migration — wiping previously migrated `certs`/`user_packets` data on every subsequent upgrade from that version. This class of data-loss bug is exactly what commit `b53abc9a0` fixes by removing the extra case label and shifting everything back by one so each case again matches its correct oldVersion entry point.

**(3) Supporting evidence.** I confirmed via `git log -p` with a script counting added `case N:` labels per version-bump commit that `00f9da2de0...` is the *only* commit in the file's entire history that added two case labels for a single `DATABASE_VERSION` increment (all 13 other bump commits added exactly one; the 2→3 bump commit that also shows two labels was a legitimate refactor from an `if` to a `switch`, not a drift). The fix commit `b53abc9a0` is also the only commit that renumbers cases without changing `DATABASE_VERSION`, and its exact magnitude (−1 shift, merging case 7/8) precisely cancels the +1 drift introduced by `00f9da2de`.

I'm highly confident in this attribution given the precise arithmetic match (one extra case added, one case removed by the fix) and the fact that no other commit in the file's history exhibits this anomaly.
